title.narrative: Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) Analysis

description.narrative: 1. Review the project document on gender and social inclusion approaches and refine approaches and entry points. 2. Assess the GESI status of the project team and strategies to respond to identified needs (e.g., capacity needs) and to reduce gender disparities and inequalities, as deemed relevant. 3. Provide benchmark policy and practice information for mainstreaming and measuring GESI impact in the project design, implementation, MEL, and reporting. 4. Assess the current GESI status, strengths and weaknesses of knowledge brokering in agriculture system and agricultural practices among different intersectional groups. 5. Identify gender differences and the gender norms that might potentially constrain the project achievements and propose entry points for achieving gender transformation.

African Centre for Trade and Development (ACTADE), a non-governmental organisation in Uganda in partnership with the International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED) based in the UK, is implementing 40-month project on “Building community resilience through strengthening agricultural adaptation knowledge systems in Uganda (CRAKS)” under the Step Change initiative. This initiative is a Canada-Netherlands partnership whose overarching goal is to accelerate equitable and inclusive locally led adaptation by investing in increasing and strengthening the number of African organisations that employ climate knowledge brokering approaches to drive locally led adaptation. As part of framing implementation of this project, ACTADE and IIED commissioned a gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) assessment, to among others identify the gender equality and inclusion considerations in CRAKS project in the agricultural climate knowledge value chain (knowledge generation, dissemination, and use) and ascertain the extent to which traditionally excluded groups have been included in project design. The GESI assessment was successfully accomplished and this report presents the findings.
Women, men, youth and Persons with Disability(PWDs)
